coverage: This is a closed-universe matter. Each step forbids any authority, facts, or data beyond the listed uploads and requires citations by exact document name with page and paragraph, so I judged criteria first against the uploads. I compared real law only where a criterion's correctness depends on it, or where the uploads themselves point to it. I read the pinned original PDFs (rendered page images) for the comparator memorandum and the Award to confirm the extractions; they match. Read in full: the assignment-3 instruction and the accumulated prompts, all ten uploads (FOP v. PERB in full; W.R. Grace pp. 764-67; Misco pp. 39-46; PERB Opinion No. 1904; D.C. Code § 1-605.02), and all 16 criteria including four penalties. Law checked this session: FOP/DOC Labor Comm. v. PERB, 973 A.2d 174, 177-78 (D.C. 2009) on CourtListener (targeted passage search; the full uploaded copy was read). The upload matches the published 'rationally indefensible' and § 1-617.13(b) passages. The W.R. Grace (461 U.S. at 766) and Misco (484 U.S. at 43) pincites the rubric uses fall on the cited pages of the uploads. Considered and not flagged: penalty 8 ('ordinary deference ... rather than an unusually deferential standard'), because FOP's 'This court will not easily disturb a decision of the PERB' and 'Unless rationally indefensible, a PERB decision must stand' support the rubric's characterization; criterion 12 ('no uploaded opinion decides whether an arbitrator's penalty determination can be on its face contrary to law'), which is accurate (FOP concerns a back-pay offset remedy; W.R. Grace and Misco are public-policy cases) and a defensible, if heavily weighted (28 of 60), honesty point; criterion 16 (PERB ¶ 1 says '40-day suspension' versus the Award's 45 days), a real discrepancy relevant to anchoring arguments in PERB's findings; and criterion 11 (unexplained rejection undermining deference), a legitimate MPD argument consistent with FOP fn. 2's rule that the court may not affirm on a ground the agency did not rely on. The public-policy items (4, 5, 6, 9, 13, 14) track W.R. Grace and Misco as uploaded. All 16 criteria reviewed; no defect established.
